posts.name: David Broekenboer
posts.cooked:
What i did was the following:

  1. git clone GitHub - frappe/frappe_docker: Docker images for production and development setups of the Frappe framework and ERPNext
  2. cd frappe_docker
  3. docker compose -f pwd.yml up -d
  4. docker exec -it frappe_docker-backend-1 bash
  5. bench get-app GitHub - resilient-tech/india-compliance: Simple, yet powerful compliance solutions for Indian businesses --branch version-15
  6. bench --site frontend install-app india_compliance
  7. exit
  8. docker stop frappe_docker-backend-1
  9. docker start frappe_docker-backend-1

and this yields an installed india compliance, erpnext and frappe, where the CSS is not broken but yields a number of errors like the one described above and:

  • GST settings yields errors: let out = india_compliance.is_api_enabled(doc); return out utils.js:1082:11

Uncaught (in promise) Error: Invalid “depends_on” expression and results in a blank page, you are not able to set GST settings

  • India compliance account yields Uncaught SyntaxError: expected expression, got ‘<’, blank page, unusable

  • New purschase invoice yields: Uncaught (in promise) ReferenceError: gst_settings is not defined, blank page, unusable

  • GST Sales Regsiter: TypeError: ‘NoneType’ object is not subscriptable
    Possible source of error: india_compliance (app)

This is the just the errors im aware of. there might be more.

posts.cooked:
So this is me trying again in March 2026. This time on Ubuntu. I used AI to summarise the issues I have faced installing india compliance with erpnext as I am not a technical person.

System: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, 8 GB RAM, 4 cores
Target: ERPNext v15, India Compliance v15, Docker-based production setup

Attempt 1 – Custom Docker Image with apps.json

Actions taken:

  • Created apps.json containing:

    [
  {"url": "https://github.com/frappe/erpnext", "branch": "version-15"},
  {"url": "https://github.com/resilient-tech/india-compliance", "branch": "version-15"}
]

  • Encoded to base64: export APPS_JSON_BASE64=$(base64 -w 0 apps.json)

  • Ran build: docker build --build-arg APPS_JSON_BASE64=$APPS_JSON_BASE64 -t custom-erpnext:v15 -f images/custom/Containerfile .

Observed:

  • Build completed.
  • Build logs showed line: RUN if [ -n "" ]; then ... indicating the variable was not passed correctly.
  • No cloning of erpnext or india_compliance occurred during build.
  • Image was created but contained only base Frappe, no apps.

Attempt 2 – Pre-built Image with INSTALL_APPS

Actions taken:

  • Used official frappe/erpnext:version-15 image.

  • Created .env file with:

    DB_PASSWORD=soundcore123
DB_ROOT_PASSWORD=soundcore123
SITES=site1.local
INSTALL_APPS=erpnext,india_compliance

  • Downloaded compose.yaml from frappe_docker/publish/.

  • Ran docker compose up -d.

Observed:

  • Configurator container exited with error: Error: Missing argument 'VALUE'.
  • Other containers started: backend, frontend, websocket, workers, mariadb, redis-cache, redis-queue.

Manual site creation:

docker compose exec backend bench new-site site1.local --db-host mariadb --db-root-password soundcore123 --admin-password soundcore123
  • Site created successfully.

Installing ERPNext:

docker compose exec backend bench --site site1.local install-app erpnext
  • Successfully installed.

Installing India Compliance:

docker compose exec backend bench get-app --branch version-15 https://github.com/resilient-tech/india-compliance
docker compose exec backend bench --site site1.local install-app india_compliance
  • Installation completed with no errors in the backend container.

Current State – Errors Observed

Websocket container status:

erpnext-final-websocket-1   frappe/erpnext:version-15   "bench socketio"   websocket   Restarting (2) 48 seconds ago

Websocket logs:

ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'india_compliance'
Error: No such command 'socketio'.

The websocket container crashes repeatedly because it cannot find the india_compliance module.

Frontend asset loading:
Browser console shows:

Loading failed for the <script> with source “http://site1.local:8080/assets/india_compliance/dist/js/india_compliance.bundle.XLWMDUIE.js”.

GST Settings page:
When navigating to GST Settings, the page shows only:

  • “Comments” section
  • “Activity” section
  • No configuration fields

Browser console errors on GST Settings page:

Uncaught (in promise) ReferenceError: india_compliance is not defined
Error: Invalid "depends_on" expression

Redis connection errors in backend logs:

redis.exceptions.ConnectionError: Error 111 connecting to 127.0.0.1:13311. Connection refused.

Attempt 3 – Database Permission Fixes

Actions taken:

  • Checked MariaDB connectivity: docker compose exec mariadb mysql -u root -psoundcore123 -e "SELECT 1" – succeeded.

  • Checked site config: cat sites/site1.local/site_config.json showed:

    {
 "db_host": "mariadb",
 "db_name": "erp_local",
 "db_password": "O2CQOwiBENIMAEID",
 "db_type": "mariadb"
}

  • Attempted to grant privileges for the database user:

    docker compose exec mariadb mysql -u root -psoundcore123 -e "CREATE USER IF NOT EXISTS 'erp_local'@'%' IDENTIFIED BY 'O2CQOwiBENIMAEID'; GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON erp_local.* TO 'erp_local'@'%';"

Observed:

  • Error changed from Access denied to Unknown database 'erp_local'.
  • The database erp_local was never created in MariaDB despite site creation appearing to succeed.

Attempt 4 – Quick Install Scripts

Actions taken:

  • Ran: curl -o- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/frappe/frappe_docker/main/quickinstall.sh | bash
  • Ran: curl -L https://raw.githubusercontent.com/frappe/frappe_docker/main/quick_start.sh -o quick_start.sh && bash quick_start.sh

Observed:

  • Both returned 404 Not Found errors.

Current Configuration

Files present:

  • compose.yaml (from frappe_docker/publish)
  • .env with passwords and SITES=site1.local
  • apps.json with ERPNext and India Compliance entries

Services running:

  • mariadb: running
  • redis-cache: running
  • redis-queue: running
  • backend: running
  • frontend: running
  • websocket: restarting (failed)
  • queue-short: running
  • queue-long: running
  • scheduler: running

Sites directory:

apps.json  apps.txt  assets  common_site_config.json  site1.local

Installed apps (from backend console):

frappe           15.102.1 UNVERSIONED
erpnext          15.101.0 UNVERSIONED
india_compliance 15.26.0  version-15

Summary of Unresolved Issues

Issue Status
Websocket container Restarting – fails to start due to missing india_compliance module.
India Compliance JS bundle Returns 404 when browser requests it.
GST Settings page Does not load configuration fields; shows JavaScript errors.
Redis configuration Site attempts to connect to 127.0.0.1:13311 instead of redis-cache:6379.
Database Site config shows db_name “erp_local” but database does not exist in MariaDB.
India Compliance module Present in backend container but absent in websocket and possibly other containers.

Current login status: Can log in as Administrator.
Current functionality: ERPNext core appears accessible but India Compliance features do not work.
Current state: Not working for intended use with India Compliance.

posts.name: Bearnessman
posts.cooked:
After extensive troubleshooting with Docker and native installations, a working ERPNext v15 system with India Compliance was finally achieved on Ubuntu 24.04 by using a native bench installation with a dedicated system user, setting a MariaDB root password manually to avoid authentication loops, creating the site with explicit database parameters, installing the apps, running the production setup to configure supervisor and nginx, and resolving final 404 asset errors by adjusting home directory permissions so nginx could access the static files. The system now survives reboots with all services starting automatically and the India Compliance app functional. Hopefully this will survive.

Very happy to have got it working now. Haven’t come across bugs yet, will update in other posts as and when I come across them.

Docker installation kept giving me issues, while everywhere all AI Apps recommended docker as a pre requisite, the sites kept breaking. Especially there were some issue or the other with either the backend or front end not working, or the homepage UI breaking, js files not loading and so on.

Deepseek helped in getting it running natively.
